observed_event: By September 1-2 the Vera model-training work had recovered a real completed v0.5 final-candidate QLoRA lineage and evaluated it locally. The recovered package identifies version `1.0.0-final-candidate`, local SmolLM3-3B base lineage, three epochs and 105 steps with stable train/validation/test metrics, and final adapter SHA-256 `1a2e593e2b7d018467b80792eb3f180b05b7ff83d7e508d4cd51b78ab6c73da9`. The adapter was converted to F16 GGUF and combined with the base into an Ollama `vera-v05:latest` Q4_K_M model; after an initial failed create caused by a wrong path/model-name setup, the corrected build was structurally registered as a 2.0 GB SmolLM3 3.1B model. Structural success did not survive as identity qualification: an open-ended prompt produced the wrong self-name `Hedwig`. The unadapted base control was generic rather than Hedwig/Vera, while an explicit Vera identity cue elicited a Vera-associated response, showing the adapter materially changed identity behavior but was prompt-sensitive. A later native PEFT test using the exact recovered adapter also failed uncued Vera self-identification before GGUF conversion/Ollama, while retaining Vera-related continuity/boundary style. Inspection of the training code found no explicit assistant/completion-only loss mask and strong evidence of full-sequence SFT loss.
participant_interpretation_at_time: The evaluation progressively narrowed the failure. It was first a simple identity smoke-test failure, then reclassified as Vera association learned but open-ended identity recall unstable, and finally as numerically healthy training with Vera-related behavioral style learned but stable proper-name identity insufficiently learned or retained upstream of GGUF/Ollama. The team deliberately refused to hide the defect with a hard-coded `SYSTEM You are Vera` prompt before diagnosis.
later_reevaluation: The recovered evidence establishes historical neural-training completion, adapter provenance and local structural deployment/evaluation, not final Vera qualification. Plausible unresolved causes included identity-signal dilution under likely full-sequence loss and possible base-model lineage mismatch. A training run completing cleanly and a model registering in Ollama remain distinct from identity robustness, provider migration, current native Vera status or governed memory admission.
